correctness.rationale: Orthogonality reduces the normalized fourth moment to the squared norm of the two-sum fibers, which the modulus replacement majorizes. For the rim, double points give the diagonal squared terms; any collision between different nonrepeated unordered pairs is a cyclic parallelogram in the regular hexagon realization and is antipodal. This yields 2R²−Σx_v⁴+8Σ_(i<j)p_i p_j. The center contributes the stated quadratic terms and the six root-addition triples. For the cubic block, at unit Z the trace and determinant of the squared singular-value matrix are 3+4t and (1+t)², t=z_1z_2≤1/2. Its largest eigenvalue is increasing in t and at most 9/2; then block AM–GM gives T≤R^(3/2)/√6. All upper bounds hold with equal rim magnitudes, which the rim fourth-power bound requires at any nonzero optimum. The single-ratio derivative has one positive root (by the cubic sign pattern and sign change), a strict global maximum above a=0 and R=0. At equality all entries are nonzero: zero-fiber alignment gives inverse antipodal phases relative to the center; the (1,0)+(0,−1)=(1,−1) fiber then determines the third pair from the first two. Character phases suffice in every fiber. Reduction of [-2,2]² is injective modulo N≥5. The recorded polynomial and random check output and verify.py were inspected, not executed. Section 2 of python3 -B /workspace/review-evidence/rederive.py independently enumerated the full unequal-rim polynomial, checked the trace/determinant and derivative symbolically, and computed ρ≈1.358010942673985827 and K≈3.656289969310800222.
